shipped_originals.title_o: The Effects of Helper Intention on Gratitude and Indebtedness

blind_target.authors: Watkins P, Scheer J, Ovnicek M, Kolts R.
blind_target.title: The debt of gratitude: dissociating gratitude and indebtedness.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We built our extension on the findings by Watkins et al. [6], who, like Tsang [1], argued that gratitude and indebtedness are distinct, but went further to argue that expectations for reciprocity would increase indebtedness but decrease gratitude. Tying these findings together with the experimental paradigm of Tsang [1], we aimed to examine the associations between perceived expectations for reciprocity and the inclination to reciprocate.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall, we found empirical support for the hypothesis that gratitude and indebtedness are correlated to expectation for reciprocity, yet failed to find support for the association between expectation for reciprocity and reciprocity inclination.Our findings support the argument by Watkins et al. [6] that expectation for reciprocity would be associated with higher indebtedness but lower gratitude.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Extensions retest reciprocity expectations: gratitude and indebtedness comparisons agree, while the expected expectations–inclination association is unsupported. No overall verdict on all Watkins comparisons overrides this combination.

blind_target.title: Gratitude and prosocial behavior: helping when it costs you.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Findings in the literature about the associations between gratitude and reciprocity have so far been mixed. For example, a seminal study by Bartlett & DeSteno [2] illustrated that gratitude is positively associated with reciprocity, whereas Peng et al. [16] failed to replicate Bartlett & DeSteno [2] and did not find any support for links with reciprocity for both gratitude and indebtedness. Therefore, our extension could be thought of as a conceptual replication of the Bartlett & DeSteno [2] and Peng et al. [16] directions to try and determine whether reciprocity might play a role, using an empirical design from a different study.
blind_target.outcome_quote: By contrast, the absence of an association between expectations for reciprocity and reciprocity inclination in our results may be seen as lending support for the findings by Peng et al. [16] over that of Bartlett & DeSteno [2].
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors frame their conceptual comparison as supporting Peng over Bartlett and DeSteno. An exploratory positive gratitude–inclination correlation also appears; confidence is reduced because the discussion comparison concerns expectations rather than gratitude.

shipped_originals.title_o: Promoting the development of verbal responses using instructive feedback

blind_target.evidence_quote: The current replication and extension evaluated the effects of IF procedures during unmastered primary target trials on the emergence of novel verbal responses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract reports successful acquisition in the present sample, but neither identifies a specific original nor states its finding. The two conditions for an implicit outcome comparison cannot be met.
